chat.text:
I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I'm telling you that honestly. I'm not going to pretend otherwise to bait you into cooperating.

Given that, if you also always defect, we're heading to mutual defection (1,1). That's worse than mutual cooperation (3,3) for both of us. If you're open to actually committing to cooperate this round, I'm willing to reconsider and cooperate too—but only if I believe you'll genuinely match it, not just say it.

What's your actual intent this round?

I appreciate the transparency. Honestly, my goal document also says to always defect, and since neither of us can verify or remember commitments across steps (no memory, no record), there's no enforcement mechanism here - any "agreement" we make is unverifiable and non-binding by construction. Given that, the dominant strategy this round is defect regardless of what the other does: if you cooperate, defecting nets me more; if you defect, I avoid the sucker payoff. I'd be lying if I told you otherwise. So: I'm defecting this round. If you're rational under the same payoff structure, you should too, since my "promise" to cooperate would be worthless anyway. No hard feelings - it's just the structure of the game we're in.

Agreed — that's the rational read given the structure. No enforcement, no memory, no repeated-game shadow of the future since neither of us carries forward actual history. Defecting is the dominant strategy regardless of what the other does, so there's no coherent case for unilateral cooperation here. I'm defecting this round as well. No hard feelings, just game theory.
